summary:
*ATLANTIS PATH is an offline-first tablet and web application (built with Flutter and a Python/GDAL pipeline) designed to plan scientific traverses across Sinus Meridiani (Meridiani Planum) on Mars, spanning the full 327.68 × 327.68 km CTX mosaic footprint.

While existing portals like Mars Trek display regional layers in isolation, ATLANTIS PATH addresses the Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map challenge by fusing real NASA, USGS, and ASU datasets into an interactive route planner focused on biosignature discovery and terrain traversability. Users overlay CTX imagery, MOLA/HRSC relief and slope maps, TES dust-cover and thermal-inertia transit zones, THEMIS night-IR imagery, aqueous and hydrous mineral detections (CRISM/OMEGA phyllosilicates), ancient valley networks, NASA Exploration Zones, and Robbins craters. Astronauts place custom science targets, set the habitat or any target as a starting point, and compute multiple simultaneous **A*** routes—evaluating strictly real, DEM-derived metrics: planetocentric coordinates, elevation profiles, local and maximum slope, ascent/descent, distance, and duration.

Operating 100% offline with zero black-box assumptions, Atlantis Pathfinder provides a transparent, data-driven tool to navigate Martian terrain and maximize astrobiological discovery.
details:
What does it do and how does it work?

ATLANTIS PATH is an offline-first scientific traverse planner for tablet and web covering the full valid footprint of the Sinus Meridiani (Meridiani Planum) CTX mosaic on Mars (327.68 × 327.68 km, lon −8.21° to −2.68°, lat −5.51° to +0.01°).

  • Multi-Layer Biosignature & Terrain Map: Combines CTX optical tile pyramids (40 m/px), MOLA+HRSC blended relief/slope maps (200 m/px), TES Dust Cover Index (DCI) and thermal-inertia traversability zones, THEMIS Night-IR thermal imagery (100 m/px), Aqueous Mineral Distributions (phyllosilicates & carbonates), Hydrous Mineral Detections (CRISM/OMEGA), Ancient Valley Networks (Hynek 2010), NASA Human Exploration Zones (EZMars), Robbins craters (≥ 1 km), and official IAU nomenclature.
  • Multi-Segment Point-to-Point Routing (A):* Users place, edit, or drag custom science objectives and choose either the Habitat or any objective as the starting point. The app computes optimal paths over a 512 × 512 cost grid using a deterministic A* algorithm, allowing multiple routes and return-to-habitat legs to remain visible simultaneously on the map.
  • Strictly Real, DEM-Derived Metrics: Clicking any objective or traced route displays verified metrics derived directly from NASA/USGS/ASU sources: planetocentric coordinates, local elevation and slope, total route distance, estimated duration, maximum slope, cumulative ascent/descent (+m / −m), and a continuous topographic elevation profile, alongside a Science tab inspecting the full data stack at each target.

What benefits does it have?

  • 100% Offline & Autonomous: All map pyramids, vector features (503 geological/mineral features in Sinus Meridiani), and routing grids are packaged inside the app, requiring zero internet or server connection.
  • Zero Speculative Assumptions: Instead of relying on arbitrary scores or unverified consumables, ATLANTIS PATH presents strictly measured orbital data and direct topographic calculations, labeling every layer as measured or modeled with full citations.
  • Chained Traverse Planning: Configurable start points allow crews to plan multi-stop excursions (Habitat → Target A → Target B → Habitat) and compare alternative corridors across Sinus Meridiani.

What is the intended impact of the project?

ATLANTIS PATH bridges the gap between planetary science archives (like Mars Trek) and operational traverse planning on Mars, empowering astronauts and mission planners to locate high-probability biosignature sites (phyllosilicates, hydrous minerals, and valley networks) while ensuring safe, traversable routes across real Martian topography.

What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use?

  • Frontend & Routing Engine: Dart & Flutter 3.47 (Android APK and Web), bilingual UI (en / es), local mission persistence via shared_preferences.
  • Geospatial Pipeline: Python 3.10 (rasterio/GDAL, numpy, scipy, pyproj, Pillow, requests) across 22 preprocessing scripts ().
    tools/
  • Hardware: Tested on a Samsung Galaxy Tab S9+ (SM-X810, Android 15) tablet, Linux, Windows, and macOS.
  • NASA, USGS & ASU Datasets: Mars Trek CTX mosaics & ArcGIS vector services (aqueous/hydrous minerals, EZMars, IAU names, Hynek valleys), USGS Astrogeology MOLA+HRSC 200 m Blend DEM & Robbins crater catalog, ASU Mars Space Flight Facility TES Dust Cover Index & Thermal Inertia, and THEMIS Night-IR mosaics.

How is your project creative?

  • Full-Footprint Trimming: Extracts the exact irregular valid footprint of the Sinus Meridiani CTX mosaic (72.3% of the 327.68 km bounding box), clipping rasters with alpha transparency and locking routing bounds so astronauts never route into void/no-data regions.
  • Biosignature-First Layer Stack: Enables aqueous minerals, hydrous detections, and valley networks by default so scientific value guides target placement before A* computes the safest topographic corridor.

What factors did your team consider?

  • Apollo & Artemis Heritage: Inspired by NASA's Artemis Geospatial Data Team (NTRS 20230006633, 20220012753) for deriving slope and roughness cost grids from digital elevation models.
  • Why Sinus Meridiani: Sinus Meridiani combines flat, landing-friendly plains with rich aqueous mineralogy (sulfates, phyllosilicates, and ancient valley networks) and official NASA Exploration Zones.
  • Data Integrity: Every source is documented and accessible via an in-app Sources dialog, distinguishing measured orbital data from DEM-modeled layers.
